issues.description: Method SealSaloon.orderMeal: The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares the method as returning void (no value). In the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) the method is implemented with the signature 'public boolean orderMeal(Meal meal)'. This mismatch in the declared return type (void vs boolean) creates ambiguity for students about the correct method contract to implement and may cause automated grading or tests that expect a void method signature to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent between specification and implementation. Preferably update the solution implementation to match the UML and textual description by changing the method signature to 'public void orderMeal(Meal meal)' and removing the boolean return values (handle null checks internally). Alternatively, if the boolean return is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to show 'orderMeal(Meal): boolean' and document the meaning of the returned value so students know which signature to implement.
